exactPassages: Sidewalk cafes provided beyond the building line shall comply with the requirements of this section, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and with the projection limitations of Chapter 32 of this code.
No part of any awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment or removable platform of a sidewalk cafe shall be located:
2. So as to obstruct any exit from a building;
3. So as to obstruct any cellar access hatch or areaway;

Exception: Upon special application, the commissioner may permit an easily removable, prominently designated platform, designed in accordance with Section 3111.5, to cover a cellar entrance or areaway that is not used as a required means of egress.

Where dining surfaces for the consumption of food or drink are provided, at least 10 percent of the total number of seating and standing spaces, but not less than one, of each type of dining surfaces shall be accessible and be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

testCase.question: A restaurant proposes a sidewalk café with furniture near a building exit and cellar hatch. The owner says outdoor-dining authorization allows the exterior seats to be counted separately from the interior PACO and eliminates further accessibility review. The documents do not say whether the café is beyond the building line, enclosed, or separated from the interior seating by a Section 713 fire partition. What can be concluded from the selected Building Code passages, and what remains unresolved?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The proposal cannot be approved from the selected evidence. If it is a sidewalk café beyond the building line, BC 3111.1 requires compliance not only with Section 3111 but also with Chapter 32 and separate zoning and agency requirements; the selected evidence does not provide those outside rules. BC 3111.4 prohibits café components from obstructing a building exit or cellar hatch. Its cellar-entrance exception is not automatic: it requires a special application, an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and a cellar entrance or areaway that is not required egress. BC 3111.6 makes Chapter 11 applicable to the café and its access. BC 1108.2.9.1 requires accessible seating and standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total, with not less than one accessible space at each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed and located on a level served by an accessible route. BC 3111.7 supplies only a conditional rule for an enclosed sidewalk café: unless a Section 713 fire partition separates it from inside seating, its seating is added to the inside seating solely to determine whether a PACO is required. These passages do not establish the approved interior capacity, the treatment of every open exterior seating arrangement, property-line or operational jurisdiction, DOT authorization, electrical permitting, or overall approval.

expectedUncertainty.description: The selected passages establish several conditional Building Code constraints, but they do not establish overall approval, current agency jurisdiction, lawful seating capacity, or electrical and operational requirements.

answer.answerText:
The owner’s claim is not supported by the selected Building Code passages. If the café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with BC 3111 but also with the Zoning Resolution, applicable Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioner requirements, and Chapter 32 projection limits. The cited text does not establish that an outdoor-dining authorization itself satisfies those requirements.

Sidewalk-café awnings, enclosures, fixtures, equipment, and removable platforms may not obstruct a building exit or a cellar access hatch or areaway. A platform may cover a cellar entrance or areaway only under the narrow stated exception: special application, commissioner permission, an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under BC 3111.5, and an entrance or areaway not used as a required means of egress. Because the geometry, furniture locations, and cellar-access egress status are unknown, compliance cannot be determined.

Accessibility review is not eliminated. Sidewalk cafés and access to them must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces of each type of dining surface—but never fewer than one—must be accessible, distributed throughout the facility, and on a level accessed by an accessible route. The selected passages do not authorize a separate exterior count merely because outdoor dining is authorized.

For the limited question whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, seating in an enclosed sidewalk café must be added to interior seating unless it is separated by fire partitions complying with Section 713. Whether that rule applies remains unresolved because the record does not establish whether the café is enclosed or whether a qualifying fire partition is present. The selected text supplies no general authorization to count exterior seating separately for accessibility or other purposes.
answer.conclusion: The owner’s claim is not supported by the selected Building Code passages. If the café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with BC 3111 but also with the Zoning Resolution, applicable Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioner requirements, and Chapter 32 projection limits. The cited text does not establish that an outdoor-dining authorization itself satisfies those requirements.

supportedPoints.heading: Exit and cellar-access obstructions are prohibited
supportedPoints.explanation: No sidewalk-café awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment, or removable platform may obstruct a building exit or a cellar access hatch or areaway. A platform over a cellar entrance or areaway is allowed only upon special application and commissioner permission, when it is easily removable, prominently designated, designed in accordance with Section 3111.5, and the entrance or areaway is not used as a required means of egress.

supportedPoints.heading: Accessibility remains required
supportedPoints.explanation: Sidewalk cafés and access to them must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces of each type of dining surface, but not fewer than one, must be accessible, distributed throughout the facility, and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

supportedPoints.heading: Enclosed café seating may need to be combined with interior seating
supportedPoints.explanation: To determine whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, enclosed sidewalk-café seating must be added to interior seating unless the café seating is separated from the interior by fire partitions complying with Section 713.
